ordered_diagnoses: Cerebral Autosomal Dominant Arteriopathy with Subcortical Infarcts and Leukoencephalopathy (CADASIL)

s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive neurological decline with cerebrovascular involvement
salient_findings: Lacunar infarctions and periventricular white matter hyperintensities on MRI
Multiple cerebral microbleeds on susceptibility-weighted imaging
key_facts: 2-year history of headache, dizziness, and imbalance
History of hypertension
History of cervical disc herniation
Underwent transcatheter closure for patent foramen ovale
Family history of progressive cognitive decline and imbalance
Father died of cerebral hemorrhage at age 65
Neurological examination revealed brisk bilateral tendon reflexes
Bilateral Babinski sign present
MRI showed lacunar infarctions and periventricular white matter hyperintensities
Susceptibility-weighted imaging showed multiple cerebral microbleeds
Heterozygous mutation in the HTRA1 gene

shortlist.label: Cerebral Autosomal Dominant Arteriopathy with Subcortical Infarcts and Leukoencephalopathy (CADASIL)
shortlist.why_kept: Family history of progressive cognitive decline and imbalance, presence of lacunar infarctions and periventricular white matter hyperintensities on MRI

shortlist.label: HTRA1-related Cerebral Small Vessel Disease
shortlist.why_kept: Heterozygous mutation in the HTRA1 gene, consistent with cerebral small vessel disease presentation

shortlist.label: Cerebral Amyloid Angiopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of multiple cerebral microbleeds on susceptibility-weighted imaging, suggestive of amyloid angiopathy

shortlist.label: Hypertensive Vasculopathy
shortlist.why_kept: History of hypertension, presence of lacunar infarctions and periventricular white matter hyperintensities on MRI

shortlist.label: Atherosclerotic Disease
shortlist.why_kept: History of hypertension, presence of lacunar infarctions and periventricular white matter hyperintensities on MRI, possible contribution to cerebrovascular disease

raw.rationale: The presence of a heterozygous mutation in the HTRA1 gene, along with the clinical presentation of headache, dizziness, imbalance, and imaging findings of lacunar infarctions, periventricular white matter hyperintensities, and cerebral microbleeds, strongly supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Cerebral Autosomal Dominant Arteriopathy with Subcortical Infarcts and Leukoencephalopathy (CADASIL)
rejected.why: CADASIL is typically associated with NOTCH3 gene mutations, which is not mentioned in the case.

rejected.label: Cerebral Amyloid Angiopathy
rejected.why: This condition is more commonly associated with Alzheimer's disease pathology and apolipoprotein E epsilon4 allele, not directly linked to the HTRA1 gene mutation.

rejected.label: Hypertensive Vasculopathy
rejected.why: While the patient has a history of hypertension, the presence of a specific genetic mutation and the pattern of cerebral microbleeds suggest a more specific underlying pathology.

rejected.label: Atherosclerotic Disease
rejected.why: The patient's age and lack of mentioned risk factors for atherosclerosis (e.g., high cholesterol, smoking) make this less likely, and the genetic findings point towards a different etiology.
